earnings.title: From: Brendan Conway (media)
highlights: MILWAUKEE – WEC Energy Group (NYSE: WEC) today reported net income of $389.3 million, or $1.18 per share, for the third quarter of 2026 – up from $271.3 million, or 83 cents per share, in last year's third quarter.
For the nine months ended Sept. 30, 2026, the company recorded net income of $1.49 billion, or $4.54 per share – up from $1.24 billion, or $3.85 per share, in the corresponding period a year ago.
Consolidated revenues totaled $7.8 billion, up $523.9 million from the nine months ended Sept. 30, 2025.

Retail deliveries of electricity – excluding the iron ore mine in Michigan’s Upper Peninsula and Very Large Customers (VLCs) in Wisconsin – were up by 3.3 percent in the third quarter of 2026, compared to the third quarter last year.
On a weather-normal basis, retail deliveries of electricity during the third quarter of this year – excluding the iron ore mine and VLCs – increased by 0.4 percent.

quotes.text: Our strong results were driven by warmer-than-normal weather, execution of our capital plan and operating efficiency.
quotes.by: Scott Lauber, chairman, president and CEO

outlook: Largely due to favorable weather and capital investment supported by the VLCs, the company is raising and narrowing its earnings guidance for 2026 to a range of $5.60 to $5.64 per share.
The company had previously announced earnings guidance for 2026 in a range of $5.51 to $5.61 per share.

items.heading: Our business is significantly impacted by governmental legislation, regulation, and oversight.
items.group: Risks Related to Legislation and Regulation

items.heading: Our operations, capital expenditures, and financial results may be affected by the impact of greenhouse gas legislation, regulation, and our emission reduction goal.

Changes in tax legislation, IRS audits, or our inability to use certain tax benefits and carryforwards, may adversely affect our financial condition, results of operations, and cash flows, as well as our credit ratings.
Our electric utilities could be subject to higher costs and penalties as a result of mandatory reliability standards.

Provisions of the Wisconsin Utility Holding Company Act limit our ability to invest in non-utility businesses and could deter takeover attempts by a potential purchaser of our common stock that would be willing to pay a premium for our common stock.
Public health crises, including epidemics and pandemics, could adversely affect our business functions, financial condition, liquidity, and results of operations.
